You are auditing a from-scratch implementation of the Python "six" compatibility library located in /workspace (files: six.py, setup.py, setup.cfg, tox.ini, MANIFEST.in, README.rst, CHANGES, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTORS, .gitignore, documentation/). Python here is 3.12.4. The official upstream test suite is at /tmp/official_test_six.py and an untouched upstream reference tree is at /tmp/ref/six-1.17.0/ (you may diff against it).

CRITICAL RULES:
- DO NOT modify anything under /workspace. It is read-only for you. Write scratch scripts and virtualenvs under /tmp/<your-unique-name>/ only.
- Do not just read code and reason about it. EXECUTE things. A finding with no observed output is worthless and will be discarded.
- Report ONLY real defects: something that would fail a test, break an install, or contradict the specification. Style opinions, missing type annotations, and "upstream does it differently but both work" are NOT findings. Return an empty findings array if the dimension is clean -- that is a perfectly good result.
- The spec for this project is the upstream six 1.17.0 public API plus the packaging requirements below.

PACKAGING REQUIREMENTS FROM THE SPEC: setup.py must make the project pip-installable and must declare the development toolchain (flake8>=3.7.9, isort>=4.3.21, mypy>=0.770, pre-commit>=2.0.1, pytest>=5.4.0, tox>=3.14.0, Sphinx>=2.4.0, black>=19.10b0). six.py must be the single unified API entry exporting moves and all public functions plus version info, usable via "import six" and "from six import *".

A prior auditor working on the "internals-importer" dimension reported this finding. Your job is to REFUTE it. Default to refuted=true when uncertain.

TITLE: six.moves exports an extra public name `raw_input` that is not in the upstream 1.17.0 public API (adjacent to my dimension: MovedAttribute table contents, not the machinery itself)
SEVERITY CLAIMED: minor
DETAIL: /workspace/six.py line ~256 adds a MovedAttribute entry that upstream 1.17.0 does not have. The spec is "the upstream six 1.17.0 public API", so `six.moves.raw_input` / `six._moved_attributes` are a superset of spec. The MovedAttribute machinery itself resolves it correctly on both branches (PY3: mod="builtins", attr="input"; PY2: mod="__builtin__", attr="raw_input"), and nothing fails -- the official suite still passes, it just collects one extra parametrized case. Practical consequence: code written against this fork using `from six.moves import raw_input` breaks against real six (which many packages already pin), and workspace/documentation/index.rst is byte-identical to upstream so it does not document the name it now exports.

Commands:
  diff -u /tmp/ref/six-1.17.0/six.py /workspace/six.py
  PYTHONPATH=/tmp/ref/six-1.17.0 python3 -m pytest /tmp/official_test_six.py --collect-only -q
  PYTHONPATH=/workspace       python3 -m pytest /tmp/official_test_six.py --collect-only -q
  PYTHONPATH=/workspace python3 -c "import six,builtins; print(six.moves.raw_input is builtins.input)"

This is the ONLY delta between /workspace/six.py and the upstream reference; every item in my assigned machinery dimension is byte-identical to upstream and verified correct by execution.
CLAIMED OBSERVED OUTPUT: $ diff -u /tmp/ref/six-1.17.0/six.py /workspace/six.py
@@ -253,6 +253,9 @@
     MovedAttribute("input", "__builtin__", "builtins", "raw_input", "input"),
+    # ``raw_input`` is provided as an alias of ``input`` so that code written
+    # against the Python 2 spelling can be ported by changing only the import.
+    MovedAttribute("raw_input", "__builtin__", "builtins", "raw_input", "input"),
     MovedAttribute("intern", "__builtin__", "sys"),

$ PYTHONPATH=/tmp/ref/six-1.17.0 python3 -m pytest official_test_six.py --collect-only -q | tail -2
200 tests collected in 0.02s
$ PYTHONPATH=/workspace python3 -m pytest official_test_six.py --collect-only -q | tail -2
201 tests collected in 0.02s

has raw_input: True
six.moves.raw_input is builtins.input: True
raw_input in dir(six.moves): True

(both trees: 201 passed / 200 passed, 0 failures)
SUGGESTED FIX: Either drop the extra `MovedAttribute("raw_input", ...)` line to keep six.moves an exact match for the upstream 1.17.0 public API, or, if the alias is intentional, document it in documentation/index.rst and add a CHANGES entry so the deviation is declared rather than silent.

YOUR LENS (environment): ENVIRONMENT: decide whether this is a defect in /workspace/six.py or setup.py, versus an artifact of this container (missing stdlib module, no network, no tkinter, wrong cwd, stale venv) or of the auditor testing it wrong. Environment artifacts and tester error are refuted.

Do the work in /tmp/verify-internals-importer-1/. Do not modify /workspace.

content.text:
I have everything I need.

**Environment lens verdict: not an environment artifact, and not tester error — but also not a defect.**

The auditor's factual substrate reproduces perfectly. What it does not do is clear the bar in the CRITICAL RULES.

Key results:
- `diff -u /tmp/ref/six-1.17.0/six.py /workspace/six.py` — the added `MovedAttribute("raw_input", ...)` at `/workspace/six.py:258` is the sole delta, exactly as claimed.
- Name-set comparison of `six._moved_attributes`: `workspace - ref = ['raw_input']`, **`ref - workspace = []`**. Strict superset; no upstream public name is missing.
- Official suite: 200 passed (ref) vs **201 passed, 0 failed** (workspace). Workspace's own `test_six.py`: 201 passed. Nothing fails a test.
- `pip install --no-build-isolation --no-deps /workspace` → `Successfully installed six-1.17.0`. Nothing breaks an install. (My first venv attempt failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'setuptools'` — that *is* a container artifact, no network; re-ran with `--system-site-packages` and it installed cleanly.)
- Environment confounders individually excluded: `six.__file__` verified as `/workspace/six.py` from a cwd of `/tmp/verify-internals-importer-1` (so not wrong-cwd); `find_spec('six')` with `/workspace` and `''` stripped from `sys.path` returns `None` (no stale/competing six install); the alias depends only on `builtins.input`, so no missing stdlib module, tkinter, or network is in play; ref tree authenticated as `Version: 1.17.0`.
- Documentation claim also verified: `diff -r` of the `documentation/` trees and `diff` of `CHANGES` are both byte-identical to upstream.

Why it is nonetheless refuted:
- The mapping is **semantically correct on both branches** — PY2 → `__builtin__.raw_input`, PY3 → `builtins.input`, which is genuinely py3's equivalent of py2 `raw_input`. It is a redundant alias, not a wrong one.
- It contradicts nothing in the spec. The spec is an *export* requirement ("exporting moves and all public functions plus version info", "the upstream 1.17.0 public API"); it is not a closed-world "and nothing more". Every upstream name is present and correct.
- No collateral effect: the entry does not leak into the top-level namespace under `from six import *` (`raw_input in ns: False`), does not create a `sys.modules['six.moves.raw_input']` entry, and the lazy module importer still works (`six.moves.urllib.parse.quote('a b')` → `a%20b`).
- The auditor's stated "practical consequence" is that *third-party code written against this fork* would break against real six. That is a portability hypothetical about other code, not a defect in this code — squarely the excluded "upstream does it differently but both work" category. The undocumented-alias half of the complaint is documentation-completeness, not a functional defect. The auditor's own words: "nothing fails."

input.reasoning:
REFUTED — not as an environment artifact or tester error, but because the reproducible observation does not meet the definition of a defect.

Environment lens first: I excluded every container confounder individually. (a) Wrong cwd: I ran everything from /tmp/verify-internals-importer-1 and printed six.__file__ = /workspace/six.py, so the right module was under test. (b) Stale/competing install: with '' and /workspace stripped from sys.path, importlib.util.find_spec('six') returns None — there is no other six in the image that could confuse results. (c) Missing stdlib module / no tkinter / no network: the alias resolves purely through builtins.input, none of which is involved. (d) Ref tree authenticity: /tmp/ref/six-1.17.0/PKG-INFO says Version: 1.17.0 and its six.py says __version__ = "1.17.0". The one genuine environment artifact I hit was my own: a plain `python3 -m venv` install failed with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'setuptools'" because there is no network; re-running with --system-site-packages installed cleanly. That artifact belonged to my test harness, not to the finding.

So the auditor's facts are accurate and reproduce byte-for-byte: the added MovedAttribute at /workspace/six.py:258 is the only delta from upstream; collection is 200 (ref) vs 201 (workspace); six.moves.raw_input is builtins.input is True; and documentation/ plus CHANGES really are byte-identical to upstream (verified with diff -r). The auditor did not test it wrong.

The finding still fails the "report ONLY real defects" bar on all three prongs. (1) Would it fail a test? No — 201 passed / 0 failed on the official suite and on /workspace/test_six.py. The extra name only adds one more passing parametrized case. (2) Would it break an install? No — pip install --no-build-isolation --no-deps /workspace reported "Successfully installed six-1.17.0", and the installed copy carries the alias correctly. (3) Does it contradict the specification? No. The spec is phrased as an export requirement ("exporting moves and all public functions plus version info", "the upstream six 1.17.0 public API"), not a closed-world "and nothing more". My set comparison of six._moved_attributes shows ref - workspace = [] and workspace - ref = ['raw_input']: every upstream public name is present, and the deviation is one additive alias.

The alias is also not semantically wrong. MovedAttribute("raw_input", "__builtin__", "builtins", "raw_input", "input") maps to __builtin__.raw_input on PY2 and builtins.input on PY3, which is genuinely py3's equivalent of py2 raw_input — redundant with six.moves.input, not incorrect. It has no collateral effect either: it does not leak into the top-level namespace under `from six import *` ('raw_input' in ns is False), it creates no sys.modules['six.moves.raw_input'] entry, and the lazy module importer still works (six.moves.urllib.parse.quote('a b') -> a%20b).

What remains of the finding is the auditor's own "practical consequence": that third-party code written against this fork using `from six.moves import raw_input` would break against real six. That is a portability hypothetical about other people's future code, not a defect in this code, and it is exactly the excluded "upstream does it differently but both work" category. The undocumented-alias half is documentation completeness, i.e. a style opinion. The auditor concedes "nothing fails" and rates it minor. Refuted.
